title: A moving analytic radius absorbs the differentiated-current charge shift with an explicit budget

moving_radius.analytic_energy: For X_n=a_n(rho)H_n with a_n(rho)=rho^(2n)/n!, G_rho=sum_n X_n and partial_rho G_rho=(2/rho)sum_n nX_n.
moving_radius.parameterized_shift_bound: For every epsilon>0, S_rho=sum_n a_n(rho)sqrt(H_nH_(n+1)) <= (epsilon/4)partial_rho G_rho + (epsilon+epsilon^(-1))G_rho/(2rho).
moving_radius.proof: Rewrite each term as rho^(-1)sqrt(n+1)sqrt(X_nX_(n+1)) and use 2uv<=epsilon u^2+epsilon^(-1)v^2 before summing and reindexing.
moving_radius.radius_absorption: If dG_rho/dt<=L(t)G_rho+C_mB_A(t)S_rho on the smooth core and rho'(t)<0, choose epsilon(t)=-4rho'(t)/(C_mB_A(t)) where B_A>0. The weight derivative rho'partial_rho G absorbs the entire shifted derivative term.
moving_radius.optimized_budget: The remaining coefficient is L(t)-2rho'(t)/rho(t)+C_m^2B_A(t)^2/[8rho(t)(-rho'(t))]. Choosing -rho'=C_mB_A/4 makes epsilon=1 and leaves L+C_mB_A/rho. Thus positivity of rho is guaranteed on every interval with (C_m/4)int B_A<rho(0).
moving_radius.relation_to_k1450: This recovers a one-radius moving-energy formulation for the K1568 normal form and makes its radius expenditure explicit. It does not improve K1450's global hypothesis: an infinite B_A budget can still collapse rho.
moving_radius.scope_guard: The estimate is conditional on smooth cutoff solutions, positivity of the moving radius and integrability of the displayed coefficients. It does not prove global coefficient integrability, a positive limiting radius, gauge-invariant coercivity or a completed global PDE flow.
